_comment: This project's inputs to the shared turn-loop hooks in claude-hub/hooks/.
The mechanism lives in the hub; every string specific to this driver fork lives here.
Layered over hub defaults.json - `denies` merge by name and then FIELD BY FIELD, so a hub rule
applies here unchanged unless a field below changes it, and is deliberately not restated.

source._extensions: C/C++ firmware plus the inputs that decide what gets built. The submodule forks (src/grbl = core, src/sdcard, src/networking) sit INSIDE this tree, and that is where the real code changes live per CLAUDE.md - so their .c/.h count as source here, which is correct: a change there still has to build. 'ini' is platformio.ini, 'tpl' is platformio.tpl, 'py' is scripts/touch_build_stamp.py, 'yml' is the firmware workflow. Markdown is NOT source: CLAUDE.md and srw/README.md are documents, and demanding a firmware build after editing one would only teach me to ignore the gate.
source._ignore: Checked, and empty on purpose. The playbook's test is the INTERSECTION of what a non-human writer COMMITS with the extensions above, and nothing here intersects: .github/workflows/firmware.yml only builds and publishes a release (no `git add` back to the branch), the repo ships no commit-making script of its own, and no other project's session commits into this repo. scripts/touch_build_stamp.py writes src/build_stamp.h - a source extension - but it is gitignored, never committed and never hand-edited, and .pio/ likewise. Add an entry when a writer appears whose COMMITTED paths intersect the list above, not before.

verify._note: Firmware. There is nothing on this machine to run it on - verification here is the build that produces the .hex, and the flash-and-test is the user's, on hardware. So the gate asks for the same build CI runs, and the hand-off must say plainly what to flash and what to watch. A green build is NOT evidence the behaviour is right - say 'built, unverified on hardware - please check X' rather than 'fixed'.
verify.command: pio run -d grblHAL_Teensy4 -e teensy41     # -> .pio/build/teensy41/firmware.hex; teensy40 also builds
verify.label: firmware build (teensy41)

denies.name: flash
denies.message:
BLOCKED: flashing the Teensy was not requested in this turn's prompt.

Flashing reboots the real controller. That is hardware, and the standing rule is: cowboy about code, never about hardware that can move a gantry or burn something. Build the .hex and HAND OFF - say which file to flash with the Teensy Loader and what to watch for. If you believe a flash is needed, ask.

checklist: == TURN LOOP (c:\github\claude-hub\playbooks\turn_workflow_loop.md - canonical, follow all of it) ==
1. PLAN FIRST. Before the first Edit/Write, state in your visible response what you understood and
how you intend to do it. A plain question ("can we...", "what if...") is a DISCUSSION - answer it,
do not implement. Record it:
pwsh -File c:\github\claude-hub\tools\turn.ps1 plan "<restated ask + approach>"
2. IMPLEMENT. One AskUserQuestion call at a time. On a rename, grep the old identifier repo-wide
BEFORE the first build - this is C, so a missed reference can still link.
3. INTERIM BUILDS: pio run -d grblHAL_Teensy4 -e teensy41. Compile-checking is fine and does not
end a turn.
4. COMMIT AS YOU GO - each piece the moment it is verified. Never save commits up. A change in a
SUBMODULE is TWO commits: one in the submodule (src/grbl, src/sdcard, src/networking) and the
pointer bump here. Both, or it does not ship.
5. VERIFY = the build that produces the hex, since nothing here can run the firmware:
pio run -d grblHAL_Teensy4 -e teensy41
6. HAND OFF - name the .hex to flash (.pio/build/teensy41/firmware.hex) and say plainly what to
watch for once it is on the controller. A green build is not a working change: say
"built, unverified on hardware - please check X". The turn ends here.
THIS FORK'S SHAPE (CLAUDE.md and srw/ProposedPRs.html are canonical):
- Default branch srw/local-build-config is ALL-OR-NOTHING: it pins every submodule to its fork
branch and is the turnkey firmware. The per-submodule feat/*/fix/* branches exist for UPSTREAM
submission and cherry-pick, not for subset builds. There is no selective composer for firmware.
- The code lives in the submodule forks (core, Plugin_SD_card, Plugin_networking); this repo
carries the build config and the tracker. Know which repo you are editing before you edit it.
- srw/ProposedPRs.html is the per-PR tracker - update it when a PR's state changes.
- Pair with the ioSender and Simulator forks, but that is a SEPARATE session in that repo.
One project per session, or the conversation log files under the wrong project.
HARD RULE (hook-enforced): no flashing the Teensy unless asked THIS turn. Build and hand off.
